title: Stream and function-call translation layer for OpenAI Chat Completions (request/response fidelity)
creator: Maya Chen
description: Implement a translation layer that maps Redwood's native streaming and structured-toolcall primitives to and from the OpenAI Chat Completions (CC) request/response model. Goal: preserve behavior, semantics, and telemetry while keeping latency and token cost within existing SLOs.
background: Customers rely on OpenAI CC semantics for streaming SSE frames, function/tool calling and structured outputs. Our hosted API and Dedicated runtime expose different internal shapes (continuous KV cache frames, batched token slices, canonical function-call objects). There are subtle deltas in: frame ordering, chunk boundaries, content-encoding for streaming, function-call partial emissions, and error semantics. This ticket defines the mapping rules and builds the translation component used by the compatibility gateway.
design_decision_log: Use a dual-mode translator: (1) request shaper (incoming OA -> Redwood canonical) and (2) response composer (Redwood canonical -> OA CC). Keeps transformations isolated and testable.
Preserve idempotency keys and introduce per-frame sequence numbers to reconcile disparate chunking strategies between clients and runtime.

Stream: deliver SSE-like 'delta' frames to OA clients; ensure deterministic reassembly for function-call objects by buffering function metadata until 'name' plus final 'arguments' closure is observed or a timeout elapses.

Function-calls: prefer explicit function invocation object for OA 'function_call' vs. Redwood internal tooling hooks. Translate metadata (request ids, toolchain tags) into OA-compatible top-level fields using a namespaced header to avoid collisions.
Errors: failures during conversion must surface as OA error frames with diagnostic metadata but omit sensitive internal traces (redact stack and internal hostnames).
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Spike completed comparing OA SSE frame samples to Redwood streaming payloads. Observed differences in chunk boundary placement under batching.
2026-03-04: Prototype request shaper implemented (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/compatibility/pull/412). Basic request translation passes unit tests for 80% of test corpus.
2026-03-06: Added per-frame seqno and reassembly buffer; integration test with dedicated runtime demonstrates correct function-call reconstitution across batched token slices.
2026-03-08: Began end-to-end load test on staging; observed 2.4% p99 latency increase when using synchronous translation path. Exploring async-path to mitigate.
2026-03-09: UX and PM review: agreed to preserve original client-provided message ids and echo them in OA responses for traceability.
2026-03-10: Security review kickoff; redaction rules for error frames drafted and added to spec.
acceptance_criteria: Incoming OA streaming requests (with function_call hints) are accepted and correctly mapped to Redwood canonical requests with preserved order and ids.

Clients using OA Chat Completions streaming mode receive SSE-formatted delta frames that reassemble to equivalent messages produced by Redwood runtime (text content, role, finish_reason, and function_call reconstructed).
Function-call results from tools are presented to OA clients as a single coherent function_call payload even when runtime emits interleaved partial tokens across batches.
No sensitive internal metadata leaks to OA frames; error frames are redacted and mapped to OA error codes with a diagnostic id.
Performance: p50 latency regression <= 5ms and p99 <= 20ms vs baseline for the translation layer in streaming-heavy workloads under staging load.
Comprehensive unit and integration tests cover chunk boundary cases, tool-call timeouts, user cancellation during streaming, and idempotent retries.
testing_plan: Unit tests for request shaper mapping permutations (roles, function_call: auto/none/name-only).
Replay-based integration tests: feed recorded OA client traces (50 samples) through translator and assert byte-for-byte equivalence after reassembly.
Chaos test: simulate partial TCP connections and mid-stream client disconnects; ensure translation cleans buffers and returns deterministic retry tokens.
Load test: streaming-concurrency matrix (1k, 5k, 10k simultaneous SSE sessions) to validate memory and latency SLOs.
Security test: static analysis of exported fields; redaction verification via synthetic leaked-fields attempt.
Compatibility regression suite to run nightly against public OA compatibility matrix.
rollout_plan: Stage 1: Deploy translator to staging behind feature flag 'compat-oa-cc-v2' and run full test matrix (1 week).
Stage 2: Canary in hosted (1% traffic) for 48 hours; monitor error rate, reassembly failure rate, and p99 latency.
Stage 3: 10% traffic for 24 hours, then 50% if stable. Engage customer success for any early adopters who enabled OA compatibility.
Stage 4: Graduate to default for new accounts; provide opt-out for existing customers for 30 days before forced migration.
Rollback: Canary flag + kill switch in compatibility gateway; automated rollback script to revert routing within 5 minutes.
metrics: customer-facing errors surfaced as OA error frames: goal 0 for missing function_call payloads
open_risks: Streaming reassembly under heavy batching could increase memory pressure. Mitigation: bounded reassembly window and eviction policy keyed by request id.
Edge-case: clients that expect incremental function_call 'name' followed by later 'arguments' may interpret intermediate frames as final. Mitigation: send 'is_partial' meta and train QA fixtures.
Backpressure mismatch between OA clients and Redwood batching may lead to head-of-line blocking. Plan: implement async translation pipeline and backpressure signals at gateway.
Potential behavioral divergence for older OA clients that rely on legacy error text. Add opt-in compatibility mode preserving legacy wording.
notes: This playbook aims to be the canonical reference for engineers implementing OA CC compatibility for streaming/function-calls. Keep an eye on the telemetry keys listed in 'metrics' during canary. After rollout, schedule a 2-week postmortem to capture any semantic drift items and update SDK docs accordingly.
